---
title: "Rebuild the site"
subtitle: "Refresh the data extracts after a new run, then render"
---

```{ojs}
summary = FileAttachment("java/data/summary.json").json()
```

The pages hold no results of their own. Every number, chart and map is read from the small files in
`docs/java/data/` (CSV and JSON) and the two PNGs in `docs/assets/java/`, which
`docs/scripts/export_data.py` writes from the xdssat cache. The data on this build were exported on ${summary.generated} from the cache at ${summary.cache}, with ${summary.current_run} as the current run.

## 1. Re-export the data

From the repository root, in the `climate` environment (on Windows, through `conda run`):

```bash
conda run --no-capture-output -n climate python docs/scripts/export_data.py
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--run <folder>` | the run under `XDSSAT_CACHE/runs` that the pages call current (default `java_per_cell_1991-2020_slpf0.76_rf0.58_tcldf19`) |
| `--adm1 <shp>`, `--adm2 <shp>` | admin1 and admin2 boundaries (`a2bps` codes in admin2); cut to the Java box plus 1° and simplified by 0.002° for the map overlays |
| `--skip-rasters` | skip the two 100 m PNGs and the irrigation class table (they change only when the rasters change) |
| `--skip-cli` | do not refresh the `--help` texts of the scripts |

It reads, never writes, the cache: `runs/*/` (run info, strata, onset, summary, netCDF),
`checks/districts/*_{districts,years}.csv` (from `scripts/compare_districts.py`, so run that first for a new
run), `checks/n_cultivar_sensitivity*.csv`, `obs/bdsp_*`, `soils/java.SOL`, `rasters/idn_*.tif`, and the
engine's `RICER048.CUL`. It also imports `src/config.py`, `src/sol.py`, `src/rasters.py` and
`scripts/compare_districts.py` (for `pieces()`), read only. A full export took about 95 s on the reference
machine; the extracts total about 2 MB.

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `summary.json` | current run, district comparison metrics per run (level, spatial r, trends, ...) |
| `runs.json`, `run_years.csv` | every run folder: arguments, counts, timing, yield per system and season year |
| `grid_cells.csv` | one row per weather cell of the current run: rice ha, zone, onset, mean yield, season climate, top soil layer |
| `grid_yearly.json` | yield per cell, system and season year (the netCDF explorer) |
| `nc_schema.csv`, `nc_attrs.json` | variables and global attributes of the current netCDF |
| `districts.csv`, `district_years.csv`, `java_years.csv` | the district comparison of every checked run, plus district drivers (season length, Tmin, irrigated share) |
| `provinces.geojson`, `districts.geojson`, `java_outline.geojson` | admin1 and admin2 lines drawn on every map (static PNGs too), and the Java outline that frames the maps (clockwise rings for d3) |
| `obs_*.csv` | BDSP observations for Java: province series, district means, cleaning flags |
| `sensitivity.csv`, `tcldf_cells.csv` | 40-cell sensitivity samples (N, cultivar, SOC, SLPF, TCLDF) |
| `soil_layers.csv` | soil water limits and SRGF by depth (quantiles over profiles) |
| `cultivars.csv` | IR 58 and IR 64 coefficients and their definitions |
| `settings.csv`, `cli/*.txt` | `config.SETTINGS` and every script's `--help` |

## 1b. Re-run a training notebook

Each module's notebook (`notebooks/module1.ipynb` ... `module6.ipynb`) runs the DSSAT engine on example
experiments from [DSSAT/dssat-csm-data](https://github.com/DSSAT/dssat-csm-data) and on the course's data files
in `notebooks/course-data/`, and writes the CSV files its page reads into `learn/data/<module>/`. It needs the
engine (`XDSSAT_ENGINE`), a short work folder outside OneDrive (`XDSSAT_WORK`), `dssat-csm-data` cloned next to
this repository and `xlrd` for the course's spreadsheets. Run it top to bottom in Jupyter, from the `notebooks/`
folder (kernel: the xdssat Python environment), and save it, so the page shows the new outputs.

| Notebook | Runs | Run time, roughly |
|---|---|---|
| `module1.ipynb` | maize UFGA8201, potential production and sensitivity | under a minute |
| `module2.ipynb` | soybean UFGA7901, the Griffin weather import, maturity groups, the course's coefficient sweep | under a minute |
| `module3.ipynb` | GLUE: 3 x 3,000 parameter sets on five soybean treatments and 2 x 2,000 on four Colorado maize treatments (up to 48 engine processes at once), the peanut calibration grid, soils, water-limited maize, paddy rice flood water | the longest: 17 minutes (1,040 s) measured on a workstation with 2 x 20 cores (80 logical processors) |
| `module4.ipynb` | the 1976 peanut shading study and its shade sweep, the N-limited maize exercise and its self tests, nitrogen fixation in soybean | under a minute (47 s measured) |
| `module5.ipynb` | 30-season seasonal analysis, Kadoma urea rates over 13 seasons, Niger millet over 10 | a minute or two |
| `module6.ipynb` | four crop sequences in the engine's sequence mode, up to 25 years x 15 replicates | a few minutes |

Helpers: `notebooks/learnlib.py` (running the engine, cultivar variants, observed-data files, engine soil layers,
sequences) and `notebooks/glue.py` (the GLUE port). The notebooks were executed with `nbclient`; running them in
Jupyter gives the same files. `XLEARN_GLUE_N` (an environment variable) sets fewer GLUE sets per round for a
quick test run.

## 2. Render

```bash
quarto render docs
```

On Windows, stop any local server that is serving `docs/_site/` before rendering: Quarto replaces the
folder and fails with "being used by another process" (os error 32) while a file in it is open.

Quarto 1.8 renders the pages into `docs/_site/` (gitignored). The pages run Observable JS in the
browser, notebooks are shown with their stored outputs, and `freeze: auto` is set, so nothing is computed
at render time and neither Python nor the DSSAT engine is needed for this step. To look at it locally,
serve the folder over HTTP (the browser will not load the data files from `file://`):

```bash
python -m http.server 4317 --directory docs/_site
```

## OneDrive

The repository lives in OneDrive. `docs/_site/` and `docs/.quarto/` are rewritten on every render
and are gitignored, but OneDrive still syncs them, so each render churns sync traffic. Render when needed, not
in a loop, or move the output folder outside OneDrive (`output-dir` in `docs/_quarto.yml`).

## Charts and downloads

Every chart and map has **Download SVG** and **Download PNG** buttons, from `docs/assets/js/dl.js`
(`withDownload(chart, name)`). The helper folds Plot's legend, title and caption into one standalone SVG and
draws it on a canvas at 2x for the PNG, on a white background.

Backup copies of every chart are kept as SVG and PNG, each chart in its default state, one folder per page:
the training pages in `docs/assets/training/`, the case-study pages in `docs/assets/java/` and the xdssat pages
and the home page in `docs/assets/xdssat/` (each with an `index.json`). `docs/scripts/save_charts.py` writes them
from the rendered site (serve `docs/_site` on port 8765 first): it opens each page in headless Chrome, waits for
the charts and saves what the download buttons would. `--pages` limits it to some pages. The 14 pages hold 109 charts on
this build.
